gap: No result ChatGPT got states that on 2026-11-17 most single-unit 120/240 V stations it named cannot be bought for delivery now on the maker's US store: Anker F3800 / F3800 Plus ($2,399.99), EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 ($2,799) and Jackery HomePower 3600 Pro Max ($2,099) are sold out, the Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus ($3,499) is a pre-order shipping Dec 2 and the BLUETTI Apex 300 ($1,499) ships in late January, so the ones that are actually orderable are the EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra and TITAN 5000 Plus at about $3,699 and up.
standout_why: Compared against Watt & Warden (cited; prices only the F3800 Plus at $3,199.99 and F3000, dated 11-16, shows 'Check price' for the rest, no stock or ship dates), Power Station Field Guide / powerstationpilot (cited; no prices at all, no well pumps), Spark Powered (cited; one price, Apex 300 $1,499 checked 11-14, no ship date) and BuyerSheet (cited; no prices). None gives a priced list of every single-unit 120/240 V model, none gives stock or ship status, and none sets 240 V surge side by side (DELTA Pro Ultra 10.8 kW for 10 s vs Explorer 5000 Plus with no headroom above 7,200 W).
decides: For a shopper who needs a well pump running this winter, availability, not spec, decides the pick: the cheapest per watt (Apex 300, about $0.39 per 240 V watt; F3800 Plus about $0.40) can't arrive before late January or are sold out, so the orderable single-unit answer is the DELTA Pro Ultra (7,200 W, 10.8 kW / 120 A LRA surge for 10 s, which also has the largest published motor-start margin) or the TITAN 5000 Plus at about $3,699. If the shopper can wait, Apex 300 at $1,499 is the value pick for a 1/2 to 3/4 HP pump within its 3,840 W rating and 7,680 W lifting power.
